items.title: Eddie Summers Interview, 1960-09-16
items.q: I went on a Vic Gaspar... With Vic Gaspar... I liked it and went to Mr. Vic and gave me a few lessons... Vic was still living, man. I used to tell him. He thought that Vic was about the best one and the best teacher too.

ctx.x: You didn't take any other instrument, ever played guitar or anything else? I never played anything else. The trombone. And when did you take up the trombone? 1925. 1925. 1925.
I went on a Vic Gaspar. Oh yeah. You studied with him?

With him. You know I never got to meet him. I was always going to even the day or the week that he died. I had written down on a piece of paper. I was going to go by and try to see him. And I heard suddenly he died. I knew he'd been sick. One of the best. Him and Sonny. Can you tell us more about Vic? What kind of lessons he gave you? I mean what kind of a book he taught and everything that you can remember about him? He taught the white excelsior. The white excelsior? The excelsior book. I have an old mandolin…

items.title: Eddie Summers Interview, 1963-11-11
items.q: I went on to Mr. Vic Gaspar... And Sonny Henry gave me some, uh, lessons too... Just trombone on music.

ctx.x: I mean, where did you pick up the trouble? Well, I went on to Mr. Vic Gaspar. Yeah. Uh-huh. And Sonny Henry gave me some, uh, lessons too. Sonny Henry. Yeah. What lessons, I mean, when you say lessons, you mean in music or...? Music. Just trombone on music.
Yeah. Sonny Henry and Vic Gaspar. Who did you stay with the longest of the two down?
